questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
It was important for me that it was a destination where English was spoken on a high level so there was a good communication. 
Besides that, I wanted a destination that encountered a similar ethics standard as the one we have in Denmark.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not very easy. By the time I needed to find information upon my arrival Utrecht University site was under construction so there was minimal information to get. All my information upon arrival I received from my student counselor. You get very little information before the exchange begins, so you need to find or contact people yourself to get it.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The location and arrival time of the first day of my exchange I received by e-mail from my student counselor at Utrecht University. Before arrival, I also received my schedule for my entire exchange. On the first day, I was greeted by a woman who gave me a quick tour and showed/explained the hospital to me. Unfortunately, it was a very short tour (about 5-10min). The tour did not encounter any information about the routines of the hospital or my role as a student. All that I had to learn from the students over time. So it was very limited assistance I got on my first day.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: A folder over the normal workflow as a student and an overview of the system would have been a great help to receive on the first day.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I find housing through Facebook sites. It was a very difficult and very long-lasting process. 
But I was lucky to find accommodation for the first 8 weeks of my exchange. For the last 2 weeks, I stayed in a hostel. Student housing offers accommodations to exchange students. But they only offer it to exchange for 6 months or longer. So don't spend your time on that. 
Utrecht is a very expensive city to rent a place. You should be aware that the price is around 800-1400 euros every month. Some places a cheaper but very hard to find.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I got to live nearby the city center of Utrecht and experience the city. The city is very beautiful and filled with lovely restaurants, bars, and local shops. I can definitely recommend living off campus.
But don't just search for accommodation in the city center, search in all Utrecht, even search in the areas outside of Utrecht. The Netherlands has excellent public transportation so it is really easy to get around in the country.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is really difficult and takes time to find a place (for me over 4 months). But keep looking, it is definitely the time worth it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very confusing. I didn't get an overview of things. I just got e-mailed when I should upload documents to the mobility service. The host institution was also very hard to get in contact with during the registration process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could always write to my student counselor at my host university if I had some questions. But the reply time was sometimes long.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It can be a little chaotic. But just follow the instruction you get from your own institution and the host institution and it will be fine. And don't be afraid to contact people with questions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were of very high quality. The teaching is very evidence-based and you work with specialists in every department.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is very similar. The student gets to receive the anamnesis and perform the exam on every patient. Thereby you discuss the patient with the specialist and together make a plan for further exams and/or therapeutic plans.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Companion animal hospital for 10 weeks.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can fully recommend the companion animal hospital. You get to perform a lot of hands-on examinations and diagnostics methods. Besides that, you also get to see a lot of different cases which you discuss very thoroughly with the specialist.

questions.answer: No one

questions.answer: Housing is very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of activities planned by the student associations club (D.S.K).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely go to the student associations club. They know all the activities who is going on.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Ask the Dutch students what to do on the weekend. The Netherlands has a lot of festivals and events on the weekend to experience. I myself went to some of the many events in Utrecht, explored the city of Utrecht, and visit other cities in the Netherlands on the weekends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easily, Netherland and Denmarks have a lot of similarities.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be very positive and outgoing on campus. Many of the Dutch students are very friendly and welcoming.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing I can recall now.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I spend a lot of time with the local Dutch students who showed me their culture. So I most appreciate the Dutch people being so friendly and welcoming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
I know it is hard to find accommodation but keep on seeking it is definitely the time worth it. 

If you have any academic questions, just ask the students you work with. 

Just jump out into it. You need to seek some things yourself in the beginning, but 9/10 times it gives a very positive response/experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are not many exchange students at Utrecht University. I, therefore, recommend spending time with the Dutch students.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To learn from all the specialists and all the nice experiences I had with the Dutch students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To find accommodation

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
